title: Railways: the Bharatiya Railway Mazdoor Sangh
author: Editorial Desk
summary: India's largest employer has its own BMS federation.
body:
The **Bharatiya Railway Mazdoor Sangh (BRMS)** is the BMS-affiliated federation of railway employees. It is listed among the BMS federations on the organisation's website.

## Why the railways matter in labour history

Indian Railways is among the largest employers in the country, with workers in track maintenance, running, signalling, workshops, stations and offices. The 1974 railway strike was one of the largest industrial actions in Indian history. The railways have also been the testing ground of many debates about pay commissions, pensions, outsourcing and privatisation.

## Issues railway unions regularly raise

- **Pension:** the demand to restore the old pension scheme for those recruited after 2004.
- **Vacancies:** filling empty safety-category posts.
- **Running staff:** duty hours and rest.
- **Outsourcing and corporatisation:** opposition to privatisation of production units and services.
- **Pay commission** recommendations and allowances.

## Recognition

Railway unions are recognised through periodic **secret ballot elections**, and the results decide which federations sit in departmental councils. BMS-affiliated unions take part in these ballots.

The railway worker, said Thengadi Ji in his time, serves the nation as truly as any soldier, because the country cannot move without him.
